title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
source: canonical Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: A substring is a run of consecutive characters within a string. Return the length of the longest substring of s in which no character appears more than once. The empty string has a longest substring of length 0.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters

examples.explanation: ban is the longest run without a repeated character
any single w is the longest substring without a repeat

hints: A window of the string is valid until the character you are about to add is already inside the window.
Keep a sliding window and remember the last position where each character appeared.
Walk the string once with a start index. When s[i] was last seen at or after start, move start to last_seen[s[i]] + 1, and update the best length at every step.
solution: Slide a window over the string while storing the last index of every character. When the character at position i was last seen at or after the window start, move the start just past that position. Track the largest window length seen. One pass: O(n) time, O(k) space for k distinct characters.
failureHint: hidden tests include the empty string, a repeat right after a long run, and one very long random string

visible.failNote: a single character counts as a substring
